Full 4-copy lines of Hakari Hanazono (019, 021, 024) give a steady supply of bodies to occupy the front line and apply pressure.
Heavy playsets of the key characters and a low energy requirement mean few hands are completely unplayable.
The Nano Eiai (012) package and Kusuri Yakuzen (013) add some support options within a simple game plan.
Fast pressure punishes slow or clumsy starts from decks that stumble through their first two turns.
weaknesses: Stat lines on the front line fall behind stronger characters in Solo Leveling, Sakamoto Days and REZ decks, so attackers lose battles and attacks stall.
Little Impact or Damage (2) means damage output is slow, giving opponents time to stabilize and race back.
Disruption is almost nonexistent, so it cannot remove blockers or stop an opponent's key setup.
Few Events and a thin trigger package leave little defensive value when it takes damage from fast Aggro-Tempo decks.

The deck has no clear finisher with Impact or Damage (2) to close quickly once it stabilizes.

strengths: Cheap Ken Kaneki bodies and Naki are easy to deploy and build the energy line on the early 1-2 AP turns.

Half-Kakuja at four copies gives a reliable BP boost that wins battles and makes bad blocks costly for opponents.
Aogiri Tree Hideout on the energy line helps meet red energy conditions, so heavy Raid turns are enabled without extra color demands.

weaknesses: Copies are split across many card numbers (Kaneki 068, 069, 070, 071, 112 and four Ayato versions), so a hand can hold the wrong Raid pairing.

It loses the tempo race to Sakamoto Days Heisuke and Taro, Jujutsu Kaisen Yuji and the Re:ZERO Rem decks, because it needs a turn to set up the Raid.
The deck has few ways to remove blockers or use Snipe, so wide boards with high BP can wall it.
Raided characters sent to the sideline take the underlying cards with them, so removal and trades cost the deck two cards of tempo at once.
Very low recent representation and no top-cut results suggest the deck lacks a polished, tested list.

The high autopilot score reflects that a good draw of cheap Kaneki bodies, Naki and Half-Kakuja played in order wins a fair share of games, though misfiling copies across card numbers and losing tempo to faster decks still punish mistakes.

strengths: Many 4-copy early characters (Kotaro Amon and Juzo Suzuya variants) make a playable energy line on turns 1-2 likely.
Kisho Arima (084) gives a strong late-game threat once the energy line is established.
Akira Mado and Hideyoshi Nagachika (091) fill out the mid-curve, so the deck rarely stalls on awkward draws.
Owl Extermination Operation provides an event-based way to swing a key battle.
Mono-red keeps energy requirements clean, so colour screw is uncommon.
weaknesses: The deck is slower than the fast Aggro-Tempo decks (Sakamoto Days - Heisuke Mashimo, Jujutsu Kaisen - Red Yuji Itadori), which pressure life before Arima arrives.
Only 3 copies of Kisho Arima mean the finisher is often missing in the games where it is needed most.
Trigger quality is weak, giving little defensive or comeback value when life is pressured.
Spreading copies across many Amon and Suzuya card numbers dilutes synergy and leaves few draw or search effects to find answers.
Low representation and no recent top-cut results suggest the deck underperforms in the current field, and its power is dated.
Few disruption tools make it hard to stop the engines of strong midrange decks such as Solo Leveling - Purple Sung Jinwoo.

strengths: Younger Toguro bodies in several forms give a sturdy front line that holds up well against slower Midrange boards.
Elder Toguro and the high-count Karasu lines provide cheap early plays to bootstrap the energy line.
Not Bad and 100 Percent of 100 Percent give the deck extra raid and power plays that can swing a mid-game exchange.
Four copies each of Sakyo and Elder Toguro give reliable mid-curve plays that avoid dead turns.
Purple's access to Raid-style swings gives it decent late-game board turnarounds when sequenced well.
weaknesses: Its spread across five Younger Toguro numbers and four Karasu numbers dilutes copy counts and leads to awkward draws missing the right raid target.
The slow start loses tempo to Sakamoto Days Heisuke and Taro, Re:ZERO Rem and Jujutsu Kaisen Yuji, which pressure life before Toguro lines come online.
Its trigger quality is mediocre, so it struggles to stabilize when life cards flip as ordinary cards instead of defensive triggers.
Matchups against strong Purple Midrange decks like Bleach Purple Ichigo and Solo Leveling Sung Jinwoo are unfavorable because they out-value it.
It has almost no tournament presence, so the list is largely untested against the current meta and shows few modern tech cards.

Its mid-curve bodies and raid swings are forgiving of small misplays, though a mistimed raid or a poor life-trigger read can cost a game.
